sqli-1.title: Hidden products via category filter
sqli-1.objective: The category filter is vulnerable to SQL injection. Display ALL products, including unreleased ones.
sqli-1.hint: Intercept the category filter request and add: category=Gifts' OR 1=1 --

sqli-2.title: Login bypass
sqli-2.objective: Log in as the administrator user by bypassing the login form.
sqli-2.hint: Submit administrator'-- as the username and anything as the password.

sqli-3.title: UNION attack — single column
sqli-3.objective: Use a UNION attack to retrieve all usernames. The query returns a single column.
sqli-3.hint: First find column count with ' UNION SELECT NULL--, then ' UNION SELECT username FROM users--

sqli-4.title: UNION attack — two columns
sqli-4.objective: Use a UNION attack to retrieve usernames AND passwords. The query returns two columns.
sqli-4.hint: ' UNION SELECT username, password FROM users--

sqli-5.title: Blind boolean — conditional responses
sqli-5.objective: The tracking ID is injectable. Confirm the administrator user exists using conditional responses.
sqli-5.hint: In the trackingId parameter test ' AND '1'='1 vs ' AND '1'='2, then probe: ' AND (SELECT 'a' FROM users WHERE username='administrator')='a

sqli-6.title: Blind time-based
sqli-6.objective: The tracking ID is injectable. Confirm the administrator user exists using a time-based delay.
sqli-6.hint: Use ' || pg_sleep(5)-- and probe conditions like ' || (SELECT CASE WHEN (SELECT username FROM users WHERE username='administrator')='administrator' THEN pg_sleep(5) ELSE pg_sleep(0) END)--

xss-1.title: Reflected XSS into HTML
xss-1.objective: Perform a reflected XSS attack that executes JavaScript.
xss-1.hint: Submit a search term like <script>alert(1)</script> or <img src=x onerror=alert(1)>.

xss-2.title: Stored XSS in comments
xss-2.objective: Post a comment that stores executable JavaScript.
xss-2.hint: In the comment body use <script>alert(1)</script>. It renders to anyone viewing the page.

xss-3.title: DOM XSS via location.hash
xss-3.objective: Trigger a DOM-based XSS that reads from the URL hash and executes JavaScript.
xss-3.hint: Append to the lab URL: #<img src=x onerror=print()>. It runs in the victim's browser via innerHTML.

xss-4.title: Reflected XSS into attribute
xss-4.objective: Break out of an HTML attribute and execute JavaScript.
xss-4.hint: Your input lands inside an input value attribute: " onfocus=alert(1) autofocus="

xss-5.title: Stored XSS in onerror
xss-5.objective: Stored XSS that survives a filter which strips <script> tags.
xss-5.hint: <script> tags are stripped, but <img src=x onerror=alert(1)> is not.

xss-6.title: Reflected XSS — angle brackets encoded
xss-6.objective: Angle brackets are HTML-encoded but the input lands in an event-handler context.
xss-6.hint: Break out of the quoted attribute inside the h1: " onclick=alert(1) or use onmouseover.

xss-7.title: Reflected XSS into JavaScript string
xss-7.objective: Escape a JavaScript string literal to execute code. Backslashes are filtered.
xss-7.hint: Your input is inside var x = '...'. Try closing the string and executing, or close the script tag entirely with </script><script>alert(1)</script>

csrf-1.title: CSRF where no token is used
csrf-1.objective: Change the victim's email with no CSRF token present.
csrf-1.hint: Build an HTML page with a form that auto-submits to the email endpoint via POST. The victim's session cookie travels automatically.

csrf-2.title: CSRF token not validated
csrf-2.objective: The form includes a CSRF token, but the server never checks it. Change the email anyway.
csrf-2.hint: Submit a POST with a fake/absent csrf parameter — it is accepted.

csrf-3.title: CSRF where email change happens on GET
csrf-3.objective: The email endpoint accepts GET. Exploit with a simple image tag.

csrf-4.title: CSRF with Referer validation flaw
csrf-4.objective: The server rejects cross-origin Referers but accepts requests with NO Referer header.
csrf-4.hint: Add <meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer"> to your exploit page so no Referer is sent.

csrf-5.title: CSRF token only checked for form content-type
csrf-5.objective: The token is only validated when the request uses form-urlencoded content-type. Send a non-form request instead.
csrf-5.hint: A cross-origin fetch with Content-Type: text/plain (or application/json) skips the token check.

cj-1.title: Clickjacking — basic
cj-1.objective: Load the admin page in an iframe and trick the user into clicking a button.
cj-1.hint: The page has no X-Frame-Options / CSP. Build an exploit page with an invisible iframe overlay and click it.

cj-2.title: Clickjacking — frame-busting bypass
cj-2.objective: The page has frame-busting JS. Bypass it with a sandboxed iframe.
cj-2.hint: Use <iframe sandbox="allow-forms" src="..."></iframe> so the busting script never runs.

cj-3.title: Clickjacking — form pre-filling
cj-3.objective: Pre-fill the email field via a query parameter and combine with clickjacking to silently submit.
cj-3.hint: The form reads ?email= from the URL. Pre-fill it in your iframe src, then overlay a transparent submit.

pt-1.title: Path traversal — simple case
pt-1.objective: Read /etc/passwd by escaping the images directory.

pt-2.title: Path traversal — absolute path
pt-2.objective: The traversal filter blocks '..' but an absolute path is accepted.

pt-3.title: Path traversal — stripped sequences
pt-3.objective: The app strips '../' once. Bypass it with nested traversal.
pt-3.hint: Use ....//....//etc/passwd — the filter removes one '../' leaving another.

pt-4.title: Path traversal — double URL encoding
pt-4.objective: The server decodes the URL once, then the app decodes again. Use double encoding.

pt-5.title: Path traversal — start-of-path validation
pt-5.objective: The app only accepts paths starting with /var/www/images/. Escape it.

pt-6.title: Path traversal — null byte
pt-6.objective: The app appends .png and blocks plain '..'. Use a null byte to truncate.

auth-1.title: Username enumeration via different responses
auth-1.objective: Enumerate a valid username by the differing error message, then brute-force its password.
auth-1.hint: "Invalid username" vs "Incorrect password" differs. Try carlos; its password is a common word from a small list.

auth-2.title: Brute-force with IP block bypass
auth-2.objective: Login is rate-limited by IP, but the app trusts X-Forwarded-For. Bypass the block and brute-force carlos's password.
auth-2.hint: Send a new fake X-Forwarded-For header on each attempt. Try the built-in wordlist.

auth-3.title: Account lockout — reset via other user
auth-3.objective: 5 failed attempts lock an account, but any successful login resets ALL counters. Lock then unlock to brute-force.
auth-3.hint: Log in as wiener/peter to reset counters, then continue guessing carlos's password.

auth-4.title: IDOR via userId cookie
auth-4.objective: Your account is identified by a userId cookie. Access another user's account by changing it.
auth-4.hint: Change the userId cookie to 2 (carlos) or 3 (administrator) in devtools → Application → Cookies.

auth-5.title: Forged stay-logged-in cookie
auth-5.objective: The stay-logged-in cookie is base64(username:md5(password)). Forge a valid one for carlos.
auth-5.hint: Decode your own cookie to see the format. Compute md5('montoya') and base64-encode carlos:<hash>.

auth-6.title: 2FA bypass — direct navigation
auth-6.objective: The account page itself never checks the 2FA code. Log in, then jump straight to /my-account.
auth-6.hint: Log in as carlos/montoya, skip the code entry, and go directly to /lab/auth-6/my-account.

ac-1.title: Unprotected admin functionality
ac-1.objective: Access the admin panel directly with no authentication.

ac-2.title: Unprotected admin — hidden URL
ac-2.objective: The admin panel is hidden but discoverable. Access it.

ac-3.title: IDOR via query parameter
ac-3.objective: Account pages are accessed via uid in the query string. Access another user's account.

ac-4.title: IDOR via API with controllable uid
ac-4.objective: The change-email API trusts a uid field you control. Change another user's email.

ac-5.title: Access control — method-based
ac-5.objective: The admin check only applies to GET. Use another method.
ac-5.hint: Send POST to /lab/ac-5/admin (or change GET to POST).

ac-6.title: Access control — Referer-based
ac-6.objective: Admin access is granted based on the Referer header containing /admin.
ac-6.hint: Add Referer: http://example.com/admin to your request to /lab/ac-6/admin.
